description: Single-panel transmission electron micrograph (bright-field, diffraction contrast) of the dislocation structure in Fe–20% Al strained to 2–3%; no axes are present. The image is a black-line-on-grey foil view with a marked thickness/contrast gradient: the upper-left and central regions are darker, while the lower-right corner is lighter, typical of a wedge-shaped thin foil. Two families of line contrast are visible: (i) long, essentially straight or gently curved dislocation lines running roughly vertically/diagonally across the field, several of them loosely paired as close parallel pairs, and (ii) numerous short, fine elongated segments and very small closed loops scattered through the field, many attached to the ends of the straight lines. A black arrow at the right-hand side points obliquely up-and-left toward the centre of the foil, marking the imaging g vector; a black scale bar at the bottom right is labelled 0.2 µm. The caption identifies the straight lines as screw dislocations and the short segments/loops as edge dipole segments and dipole loops, imaged with the zone axis near [0 0 1] and g = 1 1 0. Read together, the micrograph demonstrates that single dislocations glide in this disordered/short-range-ordered Fe–20% Al alloy while trailing narrow edge dipoles and small dipole loops behind the screw segments.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the dislocation structure in Fe–20% Al after 2–3% strain. Long straight/gently curved dislocation lines (many loosely paired) run across a foil with a dark-to-light thickness contrast gradient; numerous short elongated dipole segments and many small closed dipole loops are attached to or trail from the straight lines. A black arrow on the right marks the imaging g = 1 1 0 vector direction (pointing obliquely up-left); a scale bar at bottom right reads 0.2 µm. No crystallographic axes or Miller indices are printed in the image.

observations.observation: The figure is a single bright-field TEM micrograph showing dark dislocation line contrast on a grey matrix with a strong foil-thickness contrast gradient (upper-left darker, lower-right lighter).
A black scale bar at the bottom-right is printed as 0.2 µm, giving the image field a length scale of a few µm.
A black arrow on the right-hand side of the micrograph marks the direction of the imaging g vector; the arrow itself carries no printed label within the image.
The dominant line contrast consists of long straight or gently curved dislocation lines running predominantly across the field, some arranged as loosely paired near-parallel lines.
Many short, fine elongated segments and numerous very small closed loops are visible, frequently attached to the ends of the straight dislocation lines.
The caption states the material is Fe–20% Al and that the image shows straight, screw dislocations, sometimes loosely paired, plus edge dipole segments and loops.
The caption states the imaging conditions are a zone axis near [0 0 1] with g = 1 1 0, the g vector being the arrowed direction.
The citing text states the structures were observed after straining the Fe–20% Al material to 2–3%.
The citing text states that the loops and dipoles are seen to be produced by trailing from the gliding screw dislocations.
The citing text states that disordered materials, or those with some short range order, deform by movement of single dislocations with Burgers vector (1/2) 1 1 1, as illustrated by Figs. 5–7.
The citing text reports that single dislocations in the 15 and 20% Al materials were generally smoothly curved with a preference for screw orientations, as shown here.
No numeric values, crystallographic indices or legend text are printed inside the micrograph itself other than the 0.2 µm scale bar.

measured_quantities: Al content of the alloy (20% Al)
unreadable_items: No legend or axis labels exist in this figure; the g-vector arrow is unlabelled in the pixels and its '1 1 0' assignment comes only from the caption
Foils thickness/contrast gradient makes the exact boundary between dark and light foil regions (and thus the thin-foil area) a subjective read
